# Early Lease Break Checklist for a New York Tenant

A practical plan for ending a 12-month lease early on **2026-08-15** because of job relocation, while keeping costs and conflict as low as possible.
**Key known terms:** lease start **2025-11-01**, rent **USD 2,100/month**, **30 days written notice**, **reletting fee = 1 month’s rent**.

## Break-Lease Action Plan and Cost Control

| Step | What to do | Why it matters | Target date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read the lease and any addenda carefully | Confirms notice method, fees, and move-out rules | Now |
| 2 | Check whether the lease has an early termination clause | Could reduce or replace disputed charges | Now |
| 3 | Send written notice of intent to vacate | Required to start the landlord’s timeline | **By 2026-07-16** |
| 4 | Ask for written confirmation of remaining charges | Prevents surprise fees and later disputes | Within 2-3 days of notice |
| 5 | Offer cooperation on re-renting | Can reduce vacancy loss and show good faith | Immediately after notice |
| 6 | Document apartment condition and move-out steps | Protects against deposit and damage claims | 1-2 weeks before move-out |
| 7 | Return keys and get a signed receipt | Proves surrender of possession | **2026-08-15** |
| 8 | Keep a written record of all messages and payments | Helps if the landlord later disputes charges | Ongoing |

### Practical timeline
- **Now to 2026-07-15:** review lease, collect relocation proof, and prepare notice.
- **By 2026-07-16:** deliver written 30-day notice.
- **After notice:** request a written payoff statement and ask how the landlord wants showings handled.
- **Before move-out:** clean, repair minor issues, photograph the unit, and schedule key return.
- **On 2026-08-15:** hand over possession, keys, and a forwarding address.

### Likely financial exposure
- **Reletting fee:** **USD 2,100**
- **Possible rent through notice period:** depends on exact notice date and move-out timing
- **Possible extra costs:** unpaid utilities, cleaning, damage beyond normal wear, or holdover rent if keys are not returned on time

### Ways to minimize loss
- Give notice as early as possible, ideally with a clear move-out date.
- Ask the landlord to re-market the unit immediately and confirm they will mitigate damages.
- Offer flexible showings and a clean, ready-to-rent apartment.
- Leave the unit in move-in condition to reduce cleaning or damage deductions.
- Keep every communication in writing and ask for itemized charges only.
- If the landlord proposes a settlement, get it in writing before paying.

## Documents to Prepare for a Clean Exit

- Lease and all addenda
- Copy of the 30-day written notice
- Proof of job relocation, such as:
  - employer transfer letter
  - new job offer letter
  - relocation notice from HR
- Move-out photos and video with date stamps
- Rent payment history
- Utility account closing confirmations
- Forwarding address
- Key return receipt or email confirmation
- Any written agreement about fees, showings, or release terms

## Landlord Email Template for Early Move-Out

Subject: Written Notice of Early Move-Out and Lease Termination Request

Dear [Landlord Name],

I am writing to provide written notice that I will be vacating the apartment at [address] on **2026-08-15** due to a job relocation.

Please treat this email as my 30-day written notice under the lease. I would appreciate written confirmation of:
- the final move-out date
- any remaining rent or fees due
- the reletting fee amount and how it will be applied
- the process for keys, inspection, and deposit return
- any steps you would like me to take to help re-rent the apartment promptly

I want to make this transition as smooth as possible and avoid any disputes. I am happy to cooperate with showings and reasonable re-rental efforts.

Please confirm receipt of this notice in writing.

Thank you,
[Your full name]
[Apartment number]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Send Notice] https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/tenant-rights-and-responsibilities.page
Action: [Button: Move-Out Checklist] https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/tenants-rights-and-responsibilities.page

- NYC tenant rights and responsibilities: https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/tenant-rights-and-responsibilities.page
- NY State tenant guidance: https://ag.ny.gov/publications/tenants-rights-guide
- NYC housing resources: https://www.nyc.gov/site/mayorspeu/resources/tenant-rights.page
